---
title: "Mathematical detail"
---

Formulas used by `PowerUtilityModel`. Notation follows Mehra and
Prescott (1985).

## Endowment

Annual consumption growth is a two-state Markov chain. Gross growth in
the two states is

$$
\lambda_1 = 1+\mu+\sigma, \qquad \lambda_2 = 1+\mu-\sigma,
$$

with symmetric transitions $\Pr(\lambda_i\to\lambda_i)=\varphi=(1+\rho)/2$
and $\Pr(\lambda_i\to\lambda_j)=1-\varphi$. Stationary weights are
$(1/2, 1/2)$. The defaults $\mu=0.018$, $\sigma=0.036$, $\rho=-0.14$
match US per-capita consumption, 1889–1978.

## Kernel

Power utility $u(C)=C^{1-\gamma}/(1-\gamma)$ gives

$$
M_j = \delta\,\lambda_j^{-\gamma}.
$$

The kernel in state $j$ depends only on that state's consumption
growth.

## Equity

The Lucas tree pays the endowment. The price-dividend ratio $q$ solves

$$
q_i = \sum_j \pi_{ij}\, \delta\,\lambda_j^{-\gamma}\, \lambda_j\, (q_j+1).
$$

Gross return from $i$ to $j$ is $\lambda_j(q_j+1)/q_i$. The bill in
state $i$ is $1/\sum_j \pi_{ij} M_j$. Unconditional means are averages
under the stationary distribution.

A levered claim replaces $\lambda_j$ in the payoff with
$\lambda_j^{\phi}$. $\phi=1$ is equity.

## The puzzle

Mehra and Prescott search $\gamma\in(0,10]$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$ and
never reach the sample pair $(E[R_f], E[R_e]-E[R_f]) \approx
(0.80\%, 6.18\%)$. High $\gamma$ raises the premium only by raising
the bill.

Source: Mehra and Prescott (1985); Cochrane, *Asset Pricing*, ch. 1.
